# action.docker_service_rollback

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Rolls a swarm service back to its previous spec, like `docker service rollback`, and waits for the rollback to complete. The service must have been updated at least once. A `docker_service` resource managing the service will plan to re-apply its configured spec afterwards.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_service_rollback.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_service_rollback" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_service_rollback.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_service_rollback.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | `string` | required |  |  | Service ID or name. |
| `timeout` | `string` | optional |  |  | How long to wait for convergence, as a Go duration. Default `5m`. |
| `wait` | `bool` | optional |  |  | Wait until the service converges (every wanted task running). Default `true`. |

## Example

```terraform
variable "rollback_reason" {
  type    = string
  default = ""
}

resource "terraform_data" "rollback" {
  count = var.rollback_reason == "" ? 0 : 1
  input = var.rollback_reason

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_service_rollback.web]
    }
  }
}

# Rolls the service back to its previous spec. Usually run on demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_service_rollback.web
action "docker_service_rollback" "web" {
  config {
    service = "web"
    timeout = "10m"
  }
}
```
